rationale:
AUTHORITY: contract.md section C2 (frozen at lane commit 4dc80c1be48308075e83af17f15fbfe7e95e6cb8) as corrected by .ufo/waves/round-23/preseal-amendment.md (written before any C2 candidate was opened or run; no C2 result observed). This is the CORRECTED case file; the original proposal at .ufo/waves/round-23/cases-proposed/CaseSetupMalformed.json is retained untouched and is not superseded in place.

CONTRACT ROW: the fixture-format paragraph of contract section C2 (contract.md lines 82-93) - 'Fixture format mori-quota-fixture-v1 (JSON object, exact keys): schema, mountinfo, paths, device_links, btrfs_sysfs' followed by 'Missing/extra top-level keys, non-absolute paths, malformed st_dev, malformed JSON, unparseable mountinfo line -> exit 2 QUOTA_SETUP (no partial verdict)'. This case takes the missing-top-level-key arm: the fixture object has schema, mountinfo, paths and btrfs_sysfs, and the device_links key is absent, so the fixture is not an exact mori-quota-fixture-v1 object and the probe must fail at setup. The preseal amendment does not supersede this clause; it reaffirms the same strictness one level down with 'Missing/extra record keys setup', so a record that itself lacked a required member would also be a setup error. Consequently the fixture below is corrected so that the missing device_links top-level key is the SINGLE defect: every other key and every record member is present, exact-typed and contract-shaped.

VERDICT: contract.md lines 132-134 - 'Verdict precedence: setup error -> 2 QUOTA_SETUP; else any enabled -> 1 QUOTA_ENABLED ...' - makes the setup error the highest-precedence outcome, evaluated before any per-path state; '(no partial verdict)' forbids emitting per-path classification records for a rejected fixture. Expected exit 2, finding_id QUOTA_SETUP, paths []. No classification-table row applies: the quota classification table (contract.md lines 108-122, as amended) is reached only after a fixture has been accepted, so this case exercises the setup gate, not the table.

DELTA FROM THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL (preseal-amendment.md, C2 final rules): the amendment adds a required fixture member 'qgroups_enabled' to each btrfs_sysfs UUID record with type bool-or-null, and states 'qgroups false must pair with enabled=null/mode=null'. The original proposal's btrfs_sysfs record carried only devices, qgroups and qgroups_mode, so under the amended rules that record was itself invalid (missing record key -> setup) and would have made the case a two-defect fixture that could no longer discriminate a lenient implementation. The corrected record therefore adds 'qgroups_enabled': null, pairing with qgroups false and qgroups_mode null exactly as the amendment requires. The record's other members are unchanged: devices ['dm-0'], qgroups false, qgroups_mode null. No other amendment clause touches this fixture: the fixture has no ext2/ext3/ext4 mount (so no ext_quota_option_unverified retagging), no duplicated covering mount point (so no ambiguous_overmount retagging), and no btrfs record with qgroups true (so the basis renaming to btrfs_qgroups_enabled does not appear in this expectation - the expected paths list is empty). The missing device_links defect, the fixture's otherwise-valid content, the expected exit 2 / QUOTA_SETUP / paths [] and the source set are all preserved unchanged from the original proposal.

FIXTURE VALIDITY UNDER THE AMENDED RULES (why every other part is deliberately valid): (a) paths are nonempty, unique and normalized absolute path/realpath pairs with no dot or dotdot components; (b) both st_dev values are canonical decimal MAJ:MIN with no sign and no leading zero other than the number 0 itself ('0:57', '259:1'); (c) the btrfs_sysfs key is a canonical UUID and its device entry is a plain nonempty basename without slash or control characters ('dm-0'); (d) the qgroups fields have exact types - qgroups is the bool false, qgroups_enabled is null, qgroups_mode is null; (e) each mountinfo line carries a separator and the last three fields (fstype, source, super options) are parsed per line, never file-wide; no line contains a backslash, so the octal-escape rule (exactly 040/011/012/134, other backslash escapes rejected as setup) is not triggered; the only trailing content is a single newline, and empty trailing lines are ignored; (f) no mount point appears twice in the mountinfo text, so the amended ambiguous_overmount refusal does not apply to either queried path - for /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin the covering mount points are '/' and '/home', each occurring once, and for /tmp they are '/' and '/tmp', each occurring once; (g) the fleet-root path's st_dev major is 0, so the amended btrfs equality skip applies and the intended device_check for that path remains btrfs_subvolume_skipped - this is the per-subvolume anonymous device, not an error (S081, fs/btrfs/inode.c at v7.2, btrfs_getattr: the reported st_dev comes from the root's anon_dev); (h) the mountinfo text is written in the field layout of S082 (Linux procfs documentation at v7.2, Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst, section 3.5 '/proc/<pid>/mountinfo - Information about mounts', lines 1965-1993: fields 1-6 at 1973-1978 with (3) major:minor 'value of st_dev for files on filesystem' at 1975 and (5) 'mount point: mount point relative to the process's root' at 1977, '(n...m) optional fields: zero or more fields of the form tag[:value]' at 1979, '(m+1) separator: marks the end of the optional fields' at 1980, '(m+2) filesystem type' at 1981, '(m+3) mount source' at 1982, '(m+4) super options: per super block options' at 1983); every line has fields 1-6, optional 'shared:N' fields, the '-' separator, then fstype, source and super options; (i) the btrfs lines use source /dev/mapper/root with subvolid/subvol super options and the xfs line uses super option noquota, the option string an XFS mount emits (S078, fs/xfs/xfs_super.c at v7.2, xfs_fs_show_options); the btrfs_sysfs shape mirrors the btrfs qgroup sysfs interface (S079, fs/btrfs/sysfs.c at v7.2: qgroup_enabled_show, qgroup_mode_show and the qgroups attribute group).

DISCRIMINATION under the amended rules: a lenient implementation that treats the absent device_links key as an empty mapping would not report a setup error. Under the amended fixture source resolution ('lookup RAW decoded source in device_links; use its mapped basename when present, otherwise basename(source); compare that basename against UUID devices lists'), the btrfs mount source /dev/mapper/root would fall back to its own basename 'root', which matches no UUID's devices list, so zero UUIDs list that device and the /home path reaches the btrfs row 'zero or several uuids list the device -> unknown, n/a, btrfs_device_unmapped'; the /tmp path reaches 'xfs, noquota and no quota key -> disabled, n/a, xfs_noquota_option'; with no enabled path and one unknown path the verdict would be exit 2 QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN with two per-path records. The correct behaviour is exit 2 QUOTA_SETUP with an empty paths list, so the case separates 'malformed fixture rejected' from 'fixture accepted and classified' on finding_id and on paths. Both outcomes carry exit code 2, so the case discriminates only if the oracle compares finding_id and the per-path list, not the exit code alone.

FIXTURE VALUES: the mount major:minor pairs (0:30 btrfs, 259:1 xfs), the path st_dev values (0:57, 259:1), the btrfs source /dev/mapper/root, the device name dm-0, the uuid and the xfs super-option string are the values recorded in the contract's own frozen real control (frozen/c2-expected-real.json, observed.fleet_root and observed.tmp); no host probe was used to derive them and no implementation, oracle or sibling case was consulted.

SOURCES RELIED ON: S078, S079, S081, S082 - S082 for the mountinfo line layout, S078 for the xfs super-option string, S079 for the btrfs_sysfs shape and the qgroups/enabled/mode members, S081 for the btrfs per-subvolume device difference. The expected verdict itself rests on the contract's fixture-format and verdict-precedence sentences and on the preseal amendment's strict key-set rules, not on any kernel source.
